audit_phase: Phase 5C — Independent Non-Flare Label Expansion & Circularity Audit

sources_audited.name: EOG Global Gas Flaring Catalog
sources_audited.provider: Earth Observation Group, Payne Institute, Colorado School of Mines / World Bank GFMR
sources_audited.spatial_precision: Point Geodetic Centroids of Identified Flaring Stacks (~10–30m)
sources_audited.timestamp_precision: Continuous Operational Persistence Baseline (Date-Bounded, Sub-Hour Valve Logs Not Available)
sources_audited.physical_basis: VIIRS Nightfire M-band dual-Planck curve fitting (T >= 1600 K)
sources_audited.circularity_justification: Uses night-time Shortwave/Midwave IR bands (M7, M8, M10, M12, M13) fitted to Planck blackbody radiation curves. Distinct physics from daytime 375m I-band thresholding.

sources_audited.name: Forest Survey of India (FSI) Large Forest Fire Monitoring System
sources_audited.provider: Forest Survey of India, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Dehradun
sources_audited.spatial_precision: Satellite Thermal Anomaly Points + Forest Beat Administrative Mask
sources_audited.physical_basis: MODIS and SNPP-VIIRS active fire thermal anomaly detections processed via NRSC Hyderabad
sources_audited.circularity_justification: FATALLY CIRCULAR: FSI alerts are generated directly from the exact same SNPP-VIIRS 375m and MODIS active fire detections that FIRMS publishes. Using FSI alerts as 'ground truth' to train an ML classifier on FIRMS is predicting satellite observations from the same satellite observations under a secondary government wrapper.

sources_audited.name: ICAR-CREAMS Crop Residue Burning Monitoring System
sources_audited.provider: Consortium for Research on Agroecosystem Monitoring and Modeling from Space, ICAR-IARI, New Delhi
sources_audited.geographic_coverage: Northern and Western India (Punjab, Haryana, UP, Rajasthan, Gujarat)
sources_audited.spatial_precision: District / Tehsil Tabular Aggregations + Active Fire Mask
sources_audited.physical_basis: Active fire detections from SNPP-VIIRS, NOAA-20, and MODIS masked by agricultural land cover
sources_audited.circularity_justification: FATALLY CIRCULAR: CREAMS active-fire counts are derived directly from MODIS/VIIRS thermal anomaly detections filtered by cropland boundaries. Zero non-satellite farm dispatch or burning permit records exist in the CREAMS data stream.

sources_audited.name: State Forest Department Field Range Inspection Logs
sources_audited.provider: Territorial Forest Divisions (e.g. Gujarat / Madhya Pradesh Forest Depts)
sources_audited.spatial_precision: Beat / Compartment Name (Textual, No Geocoded Boundary Polygons)
sources_audited.circularity_justification: Human ground patrol observation independent of satellite sensors.
sources_audited.rejection_reason: No public machine-readable API, no geocoded GPS boundary perimeters, and severe reporting delays render it unusable for automated spatial-temporal matching.

sources_audited.name: NASA MODIS MCD64A1 / VIIRS VNP64A1 Burned Area Product
sources_audited.provider: NASA LP DAAC / USGS EROS / University of Maryland
sources_audited.temporal_coverage: 2000–Present (Monthly product with Burn Day of Year)
sources_audited.timestamp_precision: Burn Day of Year (DOY) with +/- 1 to 5 day temporal uncertainty
sources_audited.physical_basis: Multi-day surface reflectance change detection (NIR/SWIR reflectance drop and charcoal deposition)
sources_audited.circularity_justification: Measures post-fire radiometric surface alteration rather than sub-pixel infrared thermal radiant flux. Physically independent retrieval mechanism.
sources_audited.semantic_limitation: Establishes that vegetation was burned. Does NOT distinguish uncontrolled wildfire from agricultural crop residue burning, pasture clearing, or industrial perimeter brush maintenance.

sources_audited.name: Wildland Fire Interagency Geospatial Services (WFIGS) Incident Perimeters
sources_audited.provider: National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC) / IRWIN / US Forest Service / DOI
sources_audited.spatial_precision: Vector Incident Perimeters mapped via Airborne Infrared (NIROPS) and Ground GPS (~10–30m)
sources_audited.timestamp_precision: Sub-Hour Incident Status & Daily Perimeter Timestamp
sources_audited.physical_basis: Incident Command System (ICS-209), airborne thermal line-scanners, ground wildland fire crews
sources_audited.circularity_justification: 100% independent of VIIRS/MODIS satellite active fire detection algorithms. Produced by certified wildland fire incident teams.
sources_audited.geographic_limitation: Restricted to United States territory. Cannot provide labels for India / Jamnagar observational datasets.

sources_audited.name: Canadian National Fire Database (CNFDB) & Large Fire Database
sources_audited.provider: Canadian Forest Service, Natural Resources Canada / CIFFC
sources_audited.spatial_precision: Agency Mapped Vector Perimeters (Aerial Sketching / GPS)
sources_audited.timestamp_precision: Ignition Date, Out Date, and Periodic Mapping Runs
sources_audited.physical_basis: Provincial and territorial wildland fire management agencies
sources_audited.circularity_justification: Independent agency fire perimeters and dispatch reports.
sources_audited.geographic_limitation: Restricted to Canadian territory. Cannot provide labels for India / Jamnagar observational datasets.
